Compliance with Ley 10/2010 risk categories and Banco de España customer diligence rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central – Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (www.rmc.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be submitted in Spanish or Spanish transcription. The name must be written in standard Latin characters; accented letters, punctuation, and ampersands are permitted only according to registry conventions. Names in foreign scripts must be transliterated into Spanish alphabet.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: names identical or phonetically similar to existing registered Spanish companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the chosen name is rejected, the applicant may file a new request with alternative names without penalty. To contest a rejection, the applicant must file a recurso de alzada with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month of the negative certification. The administrative appeal should attach the negative certificate, evidence of distinctiveness, and any written consent from companies with conflicting names.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are accepted for initial registered office registration, provided the location is a physical address in Spain where legal notifications can be served and a natural person or authorised agent can receive documents. For medical device manufacturing, a virtual office alone is insufficient; a physical operational establishment with equipment and technical capacity is required for sanitary authorisation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium (approximately 20% probability per year) due to unannounced Spanish Agency for Medicines and Health Products (AEMPS) inspections under medical device regulations, as well as SEPBLAC and tax authority site visits in the context of export license and AML compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio), Articles 20-22 (incorporation), 58-60 (registered office), 209-210 (board of directors), 214-215 (appointment of officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) and local Provincial Mercantile Registries.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Deed of Incorporation) executed before a Spanish Notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is €3,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind at incorporation. Capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account in the company's name; the deposit certificate is attached to the deed. No escrow account is required beyond the initial deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the company accepts the subscription of 3,000 shares of €1 par value each, fully paid in cash, as set forth in the incorporation deed. RESOLVED: That the registered office of the company is established at Calle de la Innovación 12, 28050 Madrid, Spain. RESOLVED: That the following persons are appointed as officers: [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED: That the officers are authorized to execute all documents and filings necessary to complete the company's registration and obtain all required licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investor Identification Number (NIE) for Non-Resident Shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish National Police (Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras) or Spanish Consulate in the shareholder's country of residence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each non-resident shareholder must apply for a NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) by submitting Form EX-15, passport copy, proof of investment purpose, and payment of the applicable fee. The NIE is issued within 1-2 weeks. For EU residents, a simpler procedure may apply.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide additional documentation (e.g., criminal record certificate from country of origin) and re-submit. Appeal to the Administrative Court if denied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Articles of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Spanish lawyer to draft the articles of incorporation, including the company name (obtain a negative name certificate from the Central Commercial Registry), registered office address, corporate purpose (including manufacturing of medical diagnostic scanners), share capital, and governance rules. The deed must be signed by all founding shareholders before a notary. The notary will verify the capital deposit certificate and issue the deed.
required_dossiers: Name certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the draft and resubmit. If the name is rejected, choose an alternative name and obtain a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Provisional Tax Identification Code (CIF) and Pay Transfer Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Local Tax Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of notarization, submit the deed to the AEAT to obtain a provisional CIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal). Simultaneously, file Modelo 600 to pay the Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (ITP-AJD) on the capital contribution (typically 1% of capital). The provisional CIF is issued immediately.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIF application is delayed, request an expedited process. For tax payment issues, correct the form and pay penalties if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) corresponding to the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, provisional CIF, and Form for registration to the Provincial Commercial Registry. The registry verifies the legality of the deed and issues a registration certificate. This step is mandatory for the company to acquire legal personality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect (defecto), correct the deed or provide additional documentation within the given period (usually 15 days). If the defect is not cured, the registration is rejected; appeal to the Directorate General of Registries and Notaries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the Incorporation in the Official Gazette (BORME)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME) - Central Commercial Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the registry automatically sends the incorporation details to BORME for publication. The publication is mandatory for third-party notice. The company must also publish the deed in a local newspaper if required by the articles.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate from the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact the registry to expedite. No remedy needed unless the publication contains errors; request correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive Tax ID (CIF) and Register for Corporate Taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Local Tax Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of registration, submit the registration certificate to the AEAT to convert the provisional CIF to a definitive one. Also register for Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), VAT (IVA), and withholding taxes using Modelo 036/037. The definitive CIF is issued immediately.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive CIF is not issued, verify that all prior steps are complete. For tax registration issues, provide additional documentation as requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Social Security and Obtain Employer Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) - Provincial Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the TGSS using Form TA.6. Obtain the employer account number (Código de Cuenta de Cotización). This is required before hiring employees. Also register the legal representative for social security contributions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact TGSS to expedite. Provide missing documents if required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria, Energía y Comercio (Regional Industry Department) and the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism (for national-level permits).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad (Activity License) and Licencia de Apertura (Opening License) for manufacturing facilities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) - Environmental Assessment Division, and regional environmental authorities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) required for manufacturing of medical devices involving electronic assembly and potential chemical use. The project must submit an EIA report to the regional environmental authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) and Spanish Law 5/2013. Wastewater discharge must meet limits for pH (6-9), COD (<500 mg/L), and heavy metals (e.g., lead < 0.5 mg/L). VOC emissions must be below 50 mg/m³. Hazardous waste handling must comply with Law 22/2011 and require authorized waste manager contracts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire department (Servicio de Extinción de Incendios) confirming compliance with NFPA and Spanish regulations (CTE). Structural load inspection by a certified engineer for the building. Occupational health and safety clearance from the Instituto Nacional de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (INSST) and regional labor authority, including workplace risk assessment and emergency plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Madrid; electronic filing and certification portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); customs and excise directorate within AEAT (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales) manages export declarations and EORI issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) engaged in medical-device manufacturing and export: Step 1 – before notarized incorporation, obtain a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) via AEAT form 036 filed by the incorporators; Step 2 – after execution of the public deed and mandatory registration in the Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry), file the definitive CIF/NIF application with form 036 within one month; the definitive NIF for a capital company follows the pattern B-8 digits-control; Step 3 – complete the mandatory Censo de Empresarios (census of business operators) on the same form 036, simultaneously making the IVA registration and the IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) enrolment for ISIC 3250 manufacturing activity before beginning operations; Step 4 – apply for an EORI number (ES+9 digits) from AEAT customs for export declarations; Step 5 – non-resident shareholders are permitted without restriction, but a Spanish tax representative may be required where the entity or non-EU owners trigger asset-holding rules; foreign entities not resident in Spain require a foreign-operator NIF (letter N prefix) to perform taxable transactions. The entire procedure is completed electronically with AEAT digital certificates, with a standard issuance time of 5-10 business days after the commercial-registry filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the SL is a Spanish tax-resident entity, taxed on worldwide income under Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) at the general rate of 25%; a reduced 20% rate applies to the first EUR 50,000 of taxable income of qualifying micro-enterprises with net turnover below EUR 1,000,000 (Ley 7/2024 reform), and a 15% rate may apply to certified innovative startups under Ley 28/2022; profits distributed to non-resident shareholders face withholding tax of 19% (20% from 1 January 2025); no flow-through or partnership-style pass-through treatment is available for an SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box equivalent; however, elections and option regimes available to an SL include: (1) option to form a consolidated tax group (régimen de consolidación fiscal) with direct or indirect 70% or greater Spanish subsidiaries, subject to prior AEAT authorization (art. 100 Ley 27/2014); (2) election for micro-enterprise reduced rates where the EUR 1M turnover and related-party conditions are met; (3) startup certification election under Ley 28/2022 for the 15% rate; (4) option to apply the territorial/offset credit method for foreign-source income with electable exemptions for qualifying foreign branch profits; (5) VAT group election (grupo de IVA) for entities with at least 50% control; (6) hybrid mismatch elections limited to the ATAD anti-hybrid mechanism – Spain does not permit unilateral entity-classification check-the-box, so hybrid structures must follow the mandatory ATAD 1 and 2 overriding rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish Value Added Tax), governed by Ley 37/1992 and Real Decreto 1624/1992; administered by AEAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de-minimis turnover threshold for Spanish-resident manufacturers: an SL must register for IVA (alta censal) before making any taxable supply; registration is compulsory regardless of revenue level under the general régime. For non-resident EU distance sellers and electronic-services providers the cross-border B2C Union scheme threshold is EUR 10,000. The simplified IVA régime and recargo de equivalencia are not available for ISIC 3250 manufacturing activities; the SL is placed in the general IVA régime with quarterly (modelo 303) or monthly (for large taxpayers and SII filers) returns and annual model 390.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Dual regime: (1) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) applies mandatorily to taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000, to VAT-group members, and to entities in the deferred-import régime; SII filers transmit invoice record data (issued, received, and capital goods) to AEAT via XML web-services API within 4 calendar days for issued invoices and 8 calendar days for received invoices, with no issuance-stamping requirement; (2) Verifactu (Real Decreto 1007/2023, applicable from 1 July 2025) obliges all B2B invoicing software to guarantee invoice integrity, traceability, and accessibility through a hash-chaining algorithm or QR code, and to transmit entries to AEAT on demand; (3) mandatory structured B2B electronic invoicing under Ley Crea y Crece remains pending final implementation order, with expected phasing for taxpayers above EUR 8,000,000 turnover and afterwards for all businesses; the SL manufacturing medical devices must therefore deploy Verifactu-compliant billing software, maintain the Libro Mayor of invoices, and be prepared for SII obligations once turnover thresholds are exceeded.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to third countries (outside the European Union) are zero-rated as exempt with credit of input VAT under art. 21.1 of Ley 37/1992, provided the goods physically leave EU territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter proves the exit; the SL must hold export status, use a valid EORI, and file the electronic DUA. Intra-EU dispatches of the ultrasound consoles to other Member States are exempt with credit under art. 25 of Ley 37/1992 subject to the customer's VIES number and the recapitulative Intrastat/VIES declarations. Related offshore services directly linked to exported goods, such as installation, calibration, training, and after-sales tele-diagnostics of the colour Doppler ultrasound console, are also zero-rated under the territoriality rules of arts. 69-70 Ley 37/1992 where performed for a non-EU recipient. The exported medical device must be lawfully placed on the market under EU MDR 2017/745 and the SL must retain the EC Declaration of Conformity to support the commercial validity of the export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration – DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) filed electronically via the AEAT customs system, including the EORI of the exporter and the HS classification of the phased-array ultrasound console.
Transport evidence evidencing EU exit within 90 days – Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or CMR (road), with terminal departure stamps or electronic exit confirmation.
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103/MT950 confirmation evidencing full and timely collection of the export proceeds from the non-EU buyer.
Commercial invoice, packing list, proforma or sales contract, Incoterms clause, and insurance certificate, referenced to the DUA export number.
Technical-legal documentary package: EC Declaration of Conformity under EU MDR 2017/745, Notified Body certificate, and serial-number provenance for the medical imaging console.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT applies a 4-year statute of limitations to VAT assessments. Where an export zero-rating claim fails the documentary or exit-evidence test, AEAT regularizes the sale, charging the 21% VAT omitted, late interest (3.75% for 2025, updated quarterly), and an infringement penalty of 50%-150% of the tax amount for grave offences under arts. 191 and 194 of the Ley General Tributaria (Ley 58/2003); failing to maintain normal books or Verifactu invoicing records triggers fixed penalties of EUR 150-EUR 6,000 per invoice (art. 201 LGT). Wrongfully obtained export VAT refunds are retrospectively clawed back with accrued interest. If the defrauded VAT or CIT amount exceeds EUR 120,000, the action constitutes criminal tax fraud under art. 305 Código Penal, exposing the directors to imprisonment of 1-6 years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of state subsidies; AEAT also applies targeted audit programmes on high-risk export chains in the medical-technology sector, including cross-border exchange of information with customs administrations at the port of exit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, acting within the framework of the European Central Bank and the European System of Central Banks; foreign-exchange and external-reporting matters are also subject to the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise and applicable European Union law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and is within the euro area single currency and Single Euro Payments Area. Current-account convertibility is unrestricted for legitimate trade, services, dividends, interest, royalties, salary payments, and other ordinary commercial transactions. Capital-account transactions are generally liberalised, including foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, acquisitions, repatriation of capital, and liquidation proceeds. Spanish banks may nevertheless require documentary evidence of the legal and commercial purpose, beneficial ownership, tax residence, source of funds, and underlying transaction under anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, payment-services, and tax-reporting rules. Profit remittances normally require distributable profits, approved annual accounts, proper corporate approvals, applicable withholding-tax analysis, and evidence that the payment is not an unlawful return of capital or disguised distribution. Payments to non-residents may trigger Spanish withholding tax unless reduced or eliminated under Spanish domestic law, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive as implemented in Spain, an applicable tax treaty, or other applicable exemption. Banks may delay or reject payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, high-risk counterparties, unusual trade flows, inadequate medical-device documentation, or unexplained third-party payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to the Banco de España, no general mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal statutory deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's commercial discretion, subject to bank terms, accounting requirements, tax rules, sanctions screening, and accurate external-trade and balance-of-payments reporting where applicable. Banks may request invoices, customs evidence, transport documents, customer identification, and proof of delivery. Intrastat obligations may apply to qualifying intra-EU movements, while customs declarations and export evidence apply to qualifying extra-EU exports. Cross-border transactions may be reportable through Banco de España external-sector information systems when applicable thresholds, reporting requests, statistical requirements, or regulated-sector rules apply; the precise reporting obligation should be confirmed with the bank and current Banco de España instructions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment operations and low to medium as a replacement for a principal Spanish commercial-bank relationship. A European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may passport services into Spain, subject to its home-state authorisation, passport notification, AML controls, safeguarding regime, and product permissions. An electronic-money institution cannot accept deposits as a bank and normally provides safeguarded payment balances rather than deposit-guaranteed bank deposits. Offshore digital EMIs without relevant European Economic Area authorisation, passporting, or an appropriate Spanish establishment should not be used for regulated payment services to or from the Spanish company. Fintech accounts may be unsuitable for capital contributions, bank guarantees, commercial letters of credit, cash pooling, high-value medical-device trade, or transactions requiring detailed bank documentary review. The company should retain a Spanish or European Economic Area credit institution for core treasury, reserve liquidity, trade finance, and contingency banking.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal rule that all directors must attend a bank branch in person. Remote onboarding may be available using qualified or other accepted electronic identification, video identification, electronic signatures, and verified corporate documents. The bank may require a physical meeting or enhanced video interview for non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, nominee arrangements, high-risk countries, unusual source-of-funds patterns, cash-intensive activity, trade-finance applications, or inability to verify identity electronically. At least one authorised signatory, ultimate beneficial owner, and controlling person should be prepared to complete live verification. The bank may also require Spanish tax identification numbers, certified translations, apostilles or legalisation, and original or bank-verified documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or multilayered ownership, failure to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, or mismatch between the shareholder register, corporate documents, and bank declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Spanish Commercial Registry extract; deed of incorporation and amendments; shareholder register or equivalent ownership evidence; ownership chart to natural persons; passports and address evidence for directors, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners; beneficial-owner declaration; tax identification numbers; and notarised, apostilled, legalised, or certified translations where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership or directors with no established Spanish operating footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; Spanish registered-office evidence; lease or service agreement; expected transaction and country matrix; customer and supplier profile; employment and logistics plan; Spanish tax registrations; licences or registrations relevant to medical-device activities; group structure; intercompany agreements; and explanation of the commercial rationale for Spanish incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of capital, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, or large initial transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board and shareholder resolutions; subscription or capital-increase documents; shareholder-loan agreement where applicable; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; bank statements; tax returns or financial statements; sale or financing documents supporting wealth origin; payment trail from the beneficial owner or documented group treasury account; and written confirmation of the intended use of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected export activity involving Latin America, high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, intermediaries, or third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer due-diligence files; distributor and agent agreements; end-user certificates; sanctions screening records; export-control classification; customs documentation; commercial invoices; purchase orders; bills of lading or airway bills; insurance documents; proof of delivery; beneficial-owner information for counterparties; anti-bribery procedures; and documented approval of any third-party payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical-device manufacturing or export activity without a coherent regulatory and product-compliance file.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Applicable European Union Medical Device Regulation analysis; manufacturer, importer, or distributor role assessment; CE-marking and conformity documentation where applicable; registration and economic-operator information; quality-management certificates; product catalogue; device classification; authorised-representative arrangements where relevant; customs classification; product-liability insurance; and evidence that the proposed activity matches the company's registered business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction volumes, currencies, or counterparties inconsistent with the declared business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast; monthly transaction-volume and value estimates; currency exposure schedule; projected gross margins; principal customer and supplier list; sample invoices and contracts; treasury policy; reconciliation controls; segregation-of-duties matrix; and escalation procedures for unusual transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions, adverse-media, corruption, tax-evasion, or high-risk-country exposure involving a director, owner, customer, supplier, or intermediary.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed enhanced-due-diligence questionnaire; independent identity and ownership verification; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; sanctions and adverse-media search records; risk assessment; senior-management approval; anti-corruption representations; contractual compliance clauses; payment restrictions; and ongoing monitoring plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cash, personal accounts, anonymous payment providers, cryptoasset platforms, or unrelated third-party accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition or tightly controlled exception policy; rationale for any exceptional payment; full counterparty verification; bank-origin payment evidence; reconciliations; invoices and contracts; tax treatment; compliance approval; and evidence that all operating receipts and disbursements are routed through accounts held in the company's legal name.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions, share-premium payments, and shareholder loans from an account held in the legal name of the documented shareholder or group treasury entity to the Spanish SL's account at an EU credit institution. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments where available and SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 cross-border payment messaging for non-SEPA currencies. State an accurate payment narrative such as 'share capital contribution', 'share premium contribution', or 'shareholder loan under agreement', and do not use generic descriptions that obscure the legal purpose. Maintain the shareholder or board resolution, subscription or loan agreement, bank confirmation, source-of-funds evidence, beneficial-owner evidence, and accounting entry. For a capital increase, coordinate the notarial deed, payment evidence, Commercial Registry filing, and any required tax or corporate records. Do not route capital through personal accounts or unrelated third parties. The receiving bank may request evidence of the commercial purpose, source of funds, tax residence, group relationship, and ultimate beneficiary before crediting or releasing the funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA scheme, subject to bank limits and sanctions screening. Use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA payments, with complete originator, beneficiary, address, bank identifier, invoice reference, currency, and purpose information. For larger or higher-risk medical-device purchases and exports, use documentary Commercial Letters of Credit subject to UCP 600, bank-confirmed letters of credit where commercially justified, documentary collections under URC 522, or open-account terms supported by credit insurance and counterparty controls. A bank may request the commercial invoice, purchase order, sales contract, customs classification, export or import declaration, transport document, insurance certificate, certificate of origin, end-user certificate, and evidence of delivery. Payment release must be consistent with sanctions, export-control, AML, tax, customs, and anti-bribery requirements. Reconcile all wires and trade-finance drawings to the general ledger, invoice, customs file, and approved treasury forecast.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for identified commercial exposures, subject to bank credit limits, documented hedging purpose, confirmation terms, valuation, collateral or margin requirements, and applicable EU financial-market rules.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility or where settlement is contractually cash-settled, subject to the bank's product approval, legal enforceability, sanctions review, suitability or appropriateness assessment, and documented underlying exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for recurring or material currency and funding exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, EMIR obligations where applicable, collateral and valuation controls, counterparty limits, and board-approved treasury policy.

Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options or option collars may be used only where the company understands premium, exercise, liquidity, accounting, and potential contingent-obligation consequences and the bank has completed the required appropriateness and documentation process.

Hedging should be limited to genuine forecast, committed, or balance-sheet exposures; speculative trading, excessive leverage, unapproved rolling positions, and hedges that cannot be reconciled to an underlying exposure should be prohibited by treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate filing penalty; failure to approve may delay filing and expose directors to liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; for accounts approved on 30 June, by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for companies exceeding EUR 6 million turnover; registry closure may occur after one year from the filing deadline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first 25 calendar days following six months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, 1 to 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger fixed penalties, late-payment surcharges of 1% to 15%, and compensatory interest; higher penalties apply where tax is unpaid or an assessment is required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information included with annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry through the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual accounts and updated whenever beneficial ownership changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate beneficial ownership information may prevent registration, trigger registry defects, and expose responsible persons to administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is generally mandatory when, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of these thresholds: EUR 2.85 million total assets, EUR 5.7 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Audit is also mandatory in specified regulated, public-interest, group, or subsidized-company circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish commercial accounting legislation; IFRS is primarily mandatory for listed consolidated groups and may apply in other permitted consolidated-accounting circumstances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain has no separate annual UBO confirmation return for an SL. The company must maintain current beneficial ownership information, report changes without undue delay, and include the applicable beneficial ownership declaration with the annual accounts filing. Beneficial ownership information must identify the natural persons ultimately owning or controlling the company.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Sole Shareholder, if applicable
Register of contracts with the sole shareholder, if applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 500-2,000 annually for registered-office, corporate-secretarial, and electronic-notification support; Spain does not generally require a resident registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 1,500-8,000 for a non-complex SL; higher fees may apply for regulated medical-device operations, group reporting, significant inventory, export activity, or complex related-party transactions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created entities on first EUR 300,000 and 20% on excess for the first two taxable periods with a positive tax base; R&D tax credit 25%; technological innovation credit 8%; indefinite NOL carryforward; certain free-depreciation rules for employment creation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) through the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) online filing portal (Sede Electrónica)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; separate quarterly advance payments are due via Modelo 202/222
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days after the six-month period following the fiscal year-end (i.e., for a 31-Dec year-end, by 25 July; for other year-ends, by the 25th of the month following the six-month post-close period)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish NIF, company name, registered address, principal activity code (CNAE) and balance sheet date of the SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box reports only the resident SL identity; non-resident shareholders are reported separately in the ownership annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book profit or loss for the fiscal period after depreciation, amortisation and provisions in the statutory annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident filing obligation; the SL is the standalone taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after permanent and temporary adjustments, including the offset of prior tax losses and tax-free balancing entries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base is computed from Spanish CIT rules; the foreign shareholder cannot claim foreign losses in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate tax liability at the applicable tax rate before deductions, exemptions and double-tax relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reduced tax rates or DTA-credits attributed to a shareholder are not applied at this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final payable or refundable amount after deductions (e.g., R&D credits, double-tax credit) and withholding credits/prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is refundable, the SL may claim refund; a foreign parent has no direct set-off right in Model 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing surcharge: 5% of the assessed amount if filed before any tax-authority demand; 10% within 15 days after formal demand, 15% within 30 days, 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Non-filing may trigger administrative assessment and penalties up to 50% of the omitted tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the tax authority of its residence State and deliver it to the Spanish paying SL before distribution. The payer files Form 216 (quarterly/annual non-resident withholding return) and retains the TRC in evidence. When a lower treaty rate is not applied at source, the foreign recipient may claim a refund using Formo 210/173 within the general statutory limitation period (possibly up to 4 years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: General domestic withholding rate 19% for interest and IP royalties to non-residents; 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive for qualifying associated EU companies (≥25% holding for at least one year); treaties commonly reduce royalties/interest to 10% or 5% (e.g., US/Spain treaty 10% interest and royalties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File are mandatory once annual turnover exceeds EUR 10 million. In all cases, if the aggregate value of related-party transactions with one counterparty or per single operation exceeds EUR 250,000, Form 232 (declaración informativa de operaciones vinculadas) must be filed. Small taxpayers under the EUR 10 million threshold may use a simplified TP summary if requested by AEAT.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No offshore ESR regime is applied as such in Spain; however art. 15 Law 27/2014 gives precedence to economic reality and prohibits result-neutral legal forms. A color-doppler device distribution SL with no personnel, premises, risks and substantive commercial activity can be recharacterised as a mere treasury/artificial entity; DAC-6 scheme notification and the doctrine of lifting the corporate veil will be applied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting sales revenue for colour Doppler ultrasound consoles, issuing or using false invoices, recording fictitious expenses, or shifting income to non-resident related parties without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax due (art. 191 LGT), plus late-payment interest. In criminal cases, art. 305 Código Penal imposes imprisonment of 1 to 4 years, a fine equal to six times the defrauded amount, and loss of public aid and licences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or beneficial owners who caused or acquiesced in the fraud are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties under art. 42 LGT. If criminal liability attaches, the court may order pretrial imprisonment, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and piercing of the corporate veil to satisfy restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Controlled Transaction Misreporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to submit Form 232 or the required TP Local/Master File when thresholds are met; using non-arm's length prices on intra-group cross-border sales (e.g., exporting scanners to a Latin American affiliate without economic justification), or inaccurately breaking down related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment increasing taxable income and other tax corrections; penalties for non-filing/incomplete Form 232 (up to EUR 10,000 per omission) plus a 15% penalty over the value of the disputed related-party transaction if false said data; interest from the date the return was due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Administrators who deliberately omitted or manipulated the TP documentation are jointly and severally liable for the assessments and penalties attributable to their malicious fault. Continued intentional mispricing may be treated as fraud, resulting in criminal prosecution for the legal representative, disqualification from holding managing roles, and preventive travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell / Artificial Structure, Money Laundering and AML disregard
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SL as a letterbox or conduit with no employees, physical office, stock, or commercial risk while channelling royalty/licence payments or distribution fees through low-tax non-resident entities; failing to verify ultimate beneficial ownership and ignoring `know-your-client` for medical-device purchasers in Latin America.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax recharacterisation, loss of taxation benefits; under art. 301 Código Penal money-laundering sanctions include imprisonment of 6 months to 6 years, fines up to three times the laundered value, and forfeiture of profits. The Bank of Spain may suspend license/trading activity and the AEAT can cancel the SL's NIF for lack of economic existence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and beneficial owners face liability for all hidden economic assets, joint civil liability for the corporate debt, criminal imprisonment for money laundering if they knowingly control the assets, orders to travel-banned presence for oral cross-examination, and enforcement of personal assets for the tax and criminal financial obligations.
